data.content_ref: inline:The problem 37aa16746f81 integrates with SRC_005 by proposing that 'cognitive friction' is not just a qualitative experience but a measurable behavioral signal. Specifically, it proposes that genuine reliability gain is evidenced by a non-uniform distribution of effort (time-spikes) that correlates with item difficulty, rather than a flat distribution characteristic of bureaucratic compliance. This relation is refuted if a panel exhibits a uniform distribution of time spent per item yet still consistently arrives at the correct outcome in complex cases, suggesting procedural fluency or lucky compliance rather than reasoning-driven reliability.
